Collect the metrics from a nested resampling run

Source: R/nested-results.R
collect_metrics.nested_results.Rd

collect_metrics() returns the nested estimate from nested_tune_grid() and the other nested functions. The nested estimate is each metric's mean over the outer folds' held-out scores.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'nested_results'
collect_metrics(x, ..., summarize = TRUE, type = c("long", "wide"))

Arguments

x

A nested_results from nested_tune_grid() or a related function.

...

Not used, and must be empty.

summarize

Whether to average the per-fold metrics (TRUE, the default) or return one row per outer fold (FALSE).

type

"long" (the default), one row per metric, or "wide", one column per metric. The wide shape drops the estimator, n, std_err and .weight. It gives an error for a metric with two estimators. It also gives an error for a metric named like a key column, such as id in the per-fold table.

Value

A tibble with .metric and .estimator. Summarized, it has one row per metric, with mean, n and std_err. Unsummarized, it has one row per outer fold and metric, with the design's fold labels first (id, and id2 on a repeated design) and .estimate. On a design weighted with tune::add_resample_weights(), it also has each fold's .weight.

Details

The estimate describes the whole procedure (tune, select, fit), not one fitted model. nested_final_fit() runs that procedure on all the data to fit the model to deploy. For a procedure chosen before seeing this estimate, it is the number to report for that model, because the model comes from the same procedure.

With summarize = FALSE, the function returns each outer fold's scores.

Only the outer folds that completed are read. Failed folds are dropped with a warning, and n counts the folds behind each row. If no fold completed, the function gives an error.

std_err is the standard error of the mean across the outer folds, as tune computes it. Do not build a confidence interval from it, because the outer folds share most of their training rows. vignette("estimate") covers how to read the standard error.

A metric scored at several evaluation times gets one row per time, in a .eval_time column.

See also

collect_metrics.nested_results_set() for a workflow-set run, compute_metrics.nested_results(), nested_final_fit()

Examples

data(mtcars)

rec <- recipes::recipe(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars) |>
  recipes::step_pca(recipes::all_predictors(), num_comp = tune::tune())
wf <- workflows::workflow(rec, parsnip::linear_reg())

set.seed(1)
folds <- nested_resamples(
  mtcars,
  outside = rsample::vfold_cv(v = 2),
  inside = rsample::vfold_cv(v = 2)
)
set.seed(2)
res <- nested_tune_grid(wf, folds, grid = data.frame(num_comp = 1:2))
# The estimate, then the per-fold scores behind it.
collect_metrics(res)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   .metric .estimator  mean     n std_err
#>   <chr>   <chr>      <dbl> <int>   <dbl>
#> 1 rmse    standard   2.98      2  0.459 
#> 2 rsq     standard   0.747     2  0.0691
collect_metrics(res, summarize = FALSE)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 4
#>   id    .metric .estimator .estimate
#>   <chr> <chr>   <chr>          <dbl>
#> 1 Fold1 rmse    standard       3.44 
#> 2 Fold1 rsq     standard       0.678
#> 3 Fold2 rmse    standard       2.52 
#> 4 Fold2 rsq     standard       0.816
